projects.name: Enhancing the resilience and livelihoods of communities in target wetland catchments through the rehabilitation of degraded ecosystems, promotion of climate-smart agricultural practices and alternative livelihoods, and strengthening of climate information services, thereby ensuring sustainable wetland management and improved adaptive capacity to climate change
projects.description: This programme main outcome is to build the resilience of communities and ecosystems in critical wetland catchments across Uganda. It directly addresses the degradation of wetland hydrology and associated landscapes through the rehabilitation of over 64,000 hectares of wetlands and natural grasslands, alongside the restoration of more than 11,000 hectares of degraded catchment areas. By constructing rainwater harvesting structures, restoring water retention facilities, and strengthening wetland management policies and by-laws, the initiative aims to restore ecosystem functionality, reduce topsoil loss, and improve water infiltration. These efforts are integrated with the promotion of climate-smart agricultural practices and alternative livelihoods, targeting over 50,000 households with a strong focus on women to diversify incomes and reduce pressure on fragile natural resources. Complementing these on-the-ground interventions, the programme strengthens the enabling environment for climate adaptation by improving access to reliable climate information and early warning systems. This involves upgrading meteorological and hydrological monitoring infrastructure, building capacity for data interpretation, and disseminating tailored forecasts and advisories to reach last-mile users, including smallholder farmers. By ensuring that 85% of men and women in the project area have access to improved climate services, the programme empowers communities to make timely decisions for agriculture and disaster risk reduction. Ultimately, this integrated approach combining ecosystem restoration, sustainable livelihoods, and enhanced climate information seeks to safeguard development gains, foster adaptive capacity, and ensure the long-term health of wetland ecosystems for both people and nature.

projects.name: Enhancing multistakeholder collaboration in waste management and circular economy in Uganda
projects.description: Uganda is facing a growing waste management crisis due to rapid urbanization, increased consumption, and inadequate infrastructure, with projections indicating a 70% rise in waste generation by 2050. Current systems are overstretched, especially in cities like Kampala, leading to environmental and public health issues. Existing policies are fragmented and lack effective coordination. To address these challenges, the project proposes establishing a National Multistakeholder Platform for Waste Management, combining a physical convening body with a digital, GIS-enabled data hub. This platform will facilitate real-time data sharing, coordinated planning, and inclusive governance by integrating government, private sector, civil society, academia, and informal waste workers. The initiative will also drive innovation through a national circular economy challenge, supporting pilot projects and business models across multiple regions, with a focus on creating green jobs for women and youth. Additional components include awareness campaigns, training, and toolkits to promote behavioral change and improve waste management standards.
